intro: Draft 3 is draft 2 ruled by DECISIONS.md D2 and D3: escutar for exaudíre in three places, and the two stylist fixes that touch only grammar (4:3 a verb supplied, 4:8 a subject named). The stylist’s other four proposals change a word, dissolve a repetition, close an ambiguity or say what the Hebrew says; they are refused and stay here as options.
Switch the wording to the stylist’s, pray it, switch back: every ruling can be overturned from this page.

verses.4:2a: Quando invoquei, {exaudivit} o Deus da minha justiça: * na tribulação {dilatasti}.
verses.4:2b: Tende piedade de mim, * e {exaudi} a minha oração.
verses.4:3: Filhos dos homens, {gravi} * por que amais a vaidade, e buscais a mentira?
verses.4:4: E sabei que o Senhor {mirificavit}: * o Senhor {exaudiet} quando eu clamar a ele.
verses.4:5: Irai-vos, e não pequeis: ‡ do que dizeis nos vossos corações, * {compungimini}.
verses.4:6: {sacrificate} de justiça, † e esperai no Senhor. * Muitos dizem: Quem nos mostra {bona}?
verses.4:8: Pelo fruto do seu trigo, vinho e azeite * {multiplicati}.

decisions.title: How far may the ear pull against the Latin?
decisions.why: Ruled overnight as DECISIONS.md D2, for Gustavo’s review. The stylist found eight of ten verses of draft 2 not yet native; the Latinist and both judges found nothing to correct. D2 is the rule under which both can be right, and draft 3 is draft 2 ruled by it.

options.label: Keep the Latin’s words, images, repetitions and ambiguities; yield to the ear on grammar and order.
options.note: D2 — the rule draft 3 and every psalm after it were made by

options.label: The Latin first. Its strangeness stays; the ear adapts, as it did to the Latin.
The ear first. Where a line shows the work of translation, fluency wins.
Verse by verse, as chosen below — and I will say in the note what the rule behind my choices is.

decisions.why: The image is width, against tribulation as a tight place. The Latin verb has no object; the Claude judge counts “espaço” a minor addition. Ruled (D8): the draft stands. Matos Soares’ “me pusestes ao largo” keeps the width better, but in Brazil “ao largo” is heard first as “at a distance, offshore”. To be looked at again with 118:32 dilatásti cor meum.

decisions.why: 74 times in the psalter, 33 of them the imperative, and a common versicle of the Office besides. The word study (words/exaudire.md) found that exáudi stands beside inténde in five verses, and inténde wants “atender” — so it recommends “escutar”. Ruled (DECISIONS.md D3): escutar — a hearing verb, as exaudíre is; atender is needed for inténde, which stands beside exáudi in 16:1, 54:2, 60:2, 140:1.

decisions.why: The Latin’s masculine plural excludes wheat, wine and oil as the subject. The Portuguese does not, and the ear waits to learn who multiplied. Ruled (D8, under D2): the stylist’s. A subject pronoun is grammar — and without it the ear takes “trigo, vinho e azeite” as what multiplied, which “a fructu” excludes.

choices.4:2a: exaudire → atender, not ouvir: under vós the imperative 'ouvi' (4:2b) is the same word as 'eu ouvi', and atender carries the ex- ('hear and grant'). Kept identical across exaudívit / exáudi / exáudiet (4:2a, 4:2b, 4:4). 'me abristes espaço' for dilatásti mihi keeps the image of width against tribulatio as a tight place; 'espaço' is the object Portuguese needs — the Claude judge counts it a minor addition. Alternatives: me destes largueza; me alargastes.
choices.4:3: gravi corde as ablative of quality: 'de coração pesado'. No verb supplied, as in the Latin; the stylist wants one ('tereis'). 'por que' for ut quid.
choices.4:4: mirificávit → fez maravilhoso, chosen so 15:3, 16:7 (Mirífica misericórdias tuas) and 30:22 can take the same verb, and so it does not collide with magnificare → engrandecer. The stylist hears it as assembled; its fix ('fez maravilhas pelo seu santo') says what the Hebrew says, not the Latin. cum clamávero → future subjunctive.
choices.4:5: First colon is 5 syllables short of the Latin (checks.py) — accepted: nolíte + infinitive is only the Latin negative imperative, and 'não queirais pecar' would pad the line with a calque. compungi-vos keeps the sting of compungi; the stylist finds it unrecognisable and offers 'arrependei-vos'. 'do que' is the regency Portuguese needs for the Latin accusative of respect. Reads under both pointings: mediant at ‡ (the app) or at *.
choices.4:6: Sacrificai um sacrifício keeps the figura etymologica; 'um' added in draft 2 because the stylist could not say 'Sacrificai sacrifício' (the Latin has the same repetition, so the repetition stays). bona plural → os bens — the back-translator notes it can be heard as possessions. osténdit taken as present.
choices.4:7: Signátum → marcada, perfect passive. Draft 1 opened 'Assinalada está…' (cognate: signum/sinal), cut to 'Marcada' when checks.py flagged +3 syllables under vós. Draft 2 puts the subject first: the stylist heard the participle-first opening as manufactured solemnity and the reorder costs no sense — but the Latin's word order is lost. Alternatives: assinalada; impressa (the coin-stamp sense in L&S).
choices.4:8: a fructu → pelo fruto (the Latin's καρποῦ, not Rahlfs' καιροῦ). Subject of multiplicáti sunt left unnamed, as in the Latin; but the Latin's masculine plural excludes wheat, wine and oil as subject, and the Portuguese does not (back-translator, stylist).
choices.4:9: in idípsum: draft 1 'juntamente' (taken from the gpt-5.5 critic) was rejected by the stylist and the Claude judge — it dangles: together with what? Draft 2 returns to 'a um só tempo', which is what ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό does with two verbs. Whether one rendering can serve 33:4, 40:7, 61:10, 73:6, 121:3 is open. dormirei / repousarei echo as dórmiam / requiéscam do.
choices.4:10: singuláriter → a sós (κατὰ μόνας): as open as the Latin about who is alone, God or me. Draft 1 'singularmente' read as essay prose to the stylist; its fix, 'só vós', closes the ambiguity and was not taken.

audit.note: Drafts 1 and 2 were made through the full pilot pipeline (dossier, interlinear, literal tier, prayed tier, stylist, judges, back-translation); see retrospective.md. prayed.v1.json and prayed.v2.json are those drafts; decisions.v2.json holds draft 2’s options as review.html had them.
Read draft 1; eight of ten verses marked not yet native. Its six proposals are the options marked “stylist”.

audit.note: v3, by the main session under Gustavo’s delegation of 2026-09-20 (DECISIONS.md D8): 4:2a, 4:2b, 4:4 atender → escutar (D3); 4:3 “até quando tereis o coração pesado?”; 4:8 “eles se multiplicaram”. No critic has read draft 3: the three changes are a glossary verb already gated in Pss 90 and 53, and two fixes the stylist itself proposed. The Hetzenauer page (p. 487) was read for this psalm during the collation.
